clue.text: Other pal made up excess

indicators.note: something made up is invented or put together afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A friend's invented story counts as one too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a glut or superabundance is more than is needed, an excess.

clue.text: Local fare?

parts.note: a local is a British pub, so its fare is the food a pub serves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' reads as regional cuisine; in Britain your local is your nearest pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: informal name for simple hot meals served in British pubs.

clue.text: Run away with girl once writer's gone

indicators.note: with the writer gone, those letters leave the girl's name

parts.note: Penelope is a girl's name
a pen is a writer, the tool that writes

explanation.surface: A young woman ran off with someone after an author left.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to elope is to run off secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Ulterior motive: what collagen database has in it?

definitions.meaning: a secret purpose behind an action

definitions.text: what collagen database has in it?
definitions.meaning: inside the words collagen database sits a list of items for a meeting, concealed

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading points to AGENDA concealed in collAGEN DAtabase.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a secret aim or plan kept from others is an ulterior motive.

clue.text: Was up on back of bronco in riding exhibition

parts.note: to be up on a horse is to ride it, so was up on means rode

indicators.note: the final letter of bronco is taken

explanation.surface: A cowboy stayed aboard a bucking horse at a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a show of horse riding and cattle roping skills by cowboys.

clue.text: Join indefinite number in outfit

indicators.note: the word in places the number inside the outfit

parts.note: a kit is a set of clothing or equipment, an outfit
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: An invitation to sign up for some uniform in a vague quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to knit is to unite or bind together, as broken bones knit.

clue.text: Old knight upset a name in Conservative party? It's not possible

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: the word in places the letters inside the others

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: An elderly knight is upset that someone has been named at a Tory do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ON into NO; 'in' puts AN inside C and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: informal phrase of refusal meaning something can't be done.

clue.text: The whole time a lot developed

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters of a lot are rearranged

explanation.surface: Over time, plenty came about.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the sum or entire amount of something.

clue.text: Commend a fine new novel

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of commend a fine take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine new piece of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: John Steinbeck's 1937 novella about migrant ranch workers.

clue.text: Made tea, we hear, for children

indicators.note: says the word for made tea is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to have made tea is to have brewed it

explanation.surface: Someone put the kettle on for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective sense: a family's young are its offspring, its brood.

clue.text: Shortage female in charge discovered in tight diet

indicators.note: found within, so the female and in-charge letters sit inside the jumbled diet
tight means drunk, so the letters of diet are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman running things finds herself short of food on a strict regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as strict but means drunk, the anagram signal; 'discovered in' then puts the female and in-charge letters inside the scrambled diet.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a shortfall, an amount by which something falls short.

clue.text: Eggs: run out by start of evening

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out

indicators.note: the opening letter of evening is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket dismissal as daylight fades, with eggs thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish eggs, especially as a mass in the ovary, are called hard roe.

clue.text: Moving, large book about Scottish island lake

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the large book's word is read backwards

parts.note: a tome is a large heavy book
Iona is an island of the Inner Hebrides
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A weighty volume on a Hebridean island and its loch, which stirs the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something moving stirs the feelings, being touching or affecting.

clue.text: Comic book character, an officer's personal servant

definitions.meaning: the DC Comics caped crusader of Gotham City
in the British army, the soldier assigned to look after an officer

explanation.surface: A superhero doubling as a military valet.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the masked hero, and the old army term for an officer's orderly.

clue.text: Violent storm encountered on the way up — bother!

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read backwards

parts.note: met means encountered
a pest is a nuisance or bother

explanation.surface: Someone caught in a gale climbing a path exclaims in irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns MET into TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tempest is a fierce storm with high winds.

clue.text: Detailed statement about harbour

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a port is a harbour

explanation.surface: A full account concerning a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal written account setting out findings in detail.

clue.text: Prove vase nicked by hawker

indicators.note: stolen and held by, so the vase goes inside the hawker

parts.note: a tout sells or pushes goods, a hawker
an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A street seller has pinched a vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to turn out a certain way is to prove to be so.

clue.text: Enter nervously following insensitive political address?

indicators.note: following puts the jumbled letters after the word for insensitive

parts.note: numb means lacking feeling

indicators.note: done in a jittery way, so the letters of enter are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone goes in jittery after a tactless politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' turns ENTER into ERTEN. Number Ten Downing Street is the British Prime Minister's official residence; the question mark flags address as a home address, not a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the residence in Downing Street is the Prime Minister's official address.

clue.text: Providing temperature in New York is fine

indicators.note: the word in places the letters inside New York's abbreviation

parts.note: if means providing or on condition that

explanation.surface: Weather report: New York is pleasant, provided it's warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: nifty means smart, neat, excellent.

clue.text: Initially ten, approximately, in trunk

indicators.note: the opening letter of ten is taken

parts.note: or so means approximately

explanation.surface: About ten items are packed in a travel chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like luggage; it is the body's trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the human body without head or limbs is the trunk.

clue.text: Make a mistake in bumper race

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words bumper race, spanning the gap

explanation.surface: Someone slips up during a big race.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to err is to go wrong or blunder.

clue.text: Spare more

definitions.meaning: additional or kept in reserve, as a spare part

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: something kept beyond need, and additional beyond the usual amount.

clue.text: Cover point perhaps made by fine senior member about island

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the island's letter goes within

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an elder is a senior member of a church or tribe

explanation.surface: A cricket position supposedly filled by a distinguished old member.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a cricket fielding position, so a player there is an example; 'perhaps' flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a player stationed at cover point in cricket is one of the side's fielding team.

clue.text: Saw Medical Officer, tot poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests being out of sorts, so the letters of tot are rearranged

explanation.surface: A parent took a sick toddler to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see; it is the noun, an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a saw is a proverb or maxim, a short saying.

clue.text: Legendary creature, until now, first in index

parts.note: yet means up to now, as in not yet

indicators.note: the opening letter of index is taken

explanation.surface: A mythical beast heading the index so far.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the abominable snowman of Himalayan folklore is a creature of legend.

clue.text: NI county players in blue

parts.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: Actors from Northern Ireland feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: feeling blue means feeling sad, dejected.
